caption: 01 · FRAME — What is the house asking the public to understand?. Write the evidenced proposition, intended audience, context, proof, exclusions, affected people, and correction condition. Separate a useful frame from a claim the available record cannot support.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what is the house asking the public to understand? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · RELATE — Which relationships carry the frame?. Map journalists, editors, critics, stylists, talent, institutions, buyers, creators, community authorities, platforms, and internal spokespeople. Record the purpose, relevant disclosure, access terms, embargo, conflicts, and who is excluded.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which relationships carry the frame? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · GOVERN — Who may say, approve, reuse, and retain what?. Define scope of services, spokesperson authority, substantiation, review time, confidential information, identity and image permissions, media and territory, archive copies, post-term use, credit, correction, takedown, and termination from the actual agreement.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who may say, approve, reuse, and retain what? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · REMEMBER — What enters the institutional record?. Preserve final releases, pitches where appropriate, media lists under proper privacy controls, approvals, corrections, placements, refusals, captions, credits, rights evidence, and decision context. The archive should record how public meaning was made—not only the resulting coverage.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

caption: Publicity can confer legitimacy while reproducing gatekeeping, extraction, favoritism, undisclosed influence, or historical erasure. More coverage is not automatically stronger institutional infrastructure. A responsible system must track who gains voice, who bears reputational risk, which claims are evidenced, and whether correction remains possible.
